clue.text: Very compact Gothick novel in authentic German (not English)

indicators.note: a novel thing is new and different, so the letters of the Gothic spelling are recast
the abbreviation for English is to be struck out of the German word

parts.note: taken as written, in its archaic spelling
echt is German for genuine or authentic

explanation.surface: A dense, tightly written Gothic novel, perhaps one translated from genuine German.
explanation.walkthrough: Echt is a German loanword in English too. 'novel' looks like the noun the whole surface is about, but it is the signal, and the archaic -ick spelling of Gothic supplies the K.
explanation.definitionFit: Chock-tight means wedged in as firmly as possible, with no room to spare: packed very compactly.

clue.text: Copper beam? Savoy may be supported on one

definitions.text: Savoy may be supported on one

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a stock is a beam, such as the crossbar of an anchor

explanation.surface: A copper beam, perhaps holding up the roof of London's Savoy hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: Savoy is a variety of crinkly-leaved cabbage, not the London hotel or theatre the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A custock is a Scots word for a cabbage stalk, which holds the head of a savoy cabbage up.

clue.text: Cheer when losing always? An unpleasant thing for the Irish

definitions.text: An unpleasant thing for the Irish

indicators.note: losing means dropping, so the word for ever falls away from the shout

parts.note: hooray is a cheer
ay, or aye, is an old word for always

explanation.surface: Supporters of a team that always loses find cheering a grim business.
explanation.definitionFit: In Irish English a hoor, from whore, is a difficult or unpleasant person or thing.

clue.text: Book in form of trimmed Grolier binder

indicators.note: a trimmed word has had its end cut off
putting letters in another form rearranges them

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for book
the name loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A book bound in the style of Jean Grolier, the Renaissance bibliophile famous for fine bindings.
explanation.walkthrough: Grolier and 'binder' both make the surface about bookbinding; the binder wanted is a person who binds someone by obligation.
explanation.definitionFit: An obliger is one who obliges, that is, who binds another by a promise or favour.

clue.text: Flexible computer idea, a stroke of genius (12, three words)

indicators.note: something flexible bends into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A versatile idea for a computer hailed as a brainwave.
explanation.definitionFit: Coup de maître is French for a master's stroke, an act of brilliance or masterstroke.

clue.text: Viewed from below, dainty Italian male accessory

indicators.note: in a down entry, read from the bottom upward the letters run backwards

parts.note: a cate is a dainty, a delicacy
It is the abbreviation for Italian

explanation.surface: A delicate Italian man's accessory, seen from underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: Cate is usually met in the plural, cates, an old word for delicacies.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie tack is a pin with a clasp that fastens a man's necktie to his shirt.

clue.text: Pork's prime piece taken from free-range pigs, not wild pigs

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the combined letters run in any order
taken from means removed out of, so the first letter goes

parts.note: the first letter of pork
the animals, without the farming description
taken as written

explanation.surface: A recipe insists the best cut of pork must come from free-range pigs, not wild boar.
explanation.walkthrough: The final 'pigs' are not animals: pig iron is cast in blocks called pigs.
explanation.definitionFit: A pig is an oblong mass of cast metal from a smelter, which is an ingot.

clue.text: Jock's possible racer was developing

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Scots for a greyhound
second meaning: past tense of a verb of growth

explanation.surface: A Scotsman's racing dog was coming on nicely.
explanation.walkthrough: Jock is a nickname for a Scot, marking a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Grew is short for grewhound, a Scots form of greyhound, the racing dog; it is also the past of grow.

clue.text: Fashionable male hummed off-key about 'nothing new in fashion' (12, three words)

indicators.note: an off-key tune strays from the right notes, so these letters stray from their order

parts.note: taken as written
O is zero, nothing

indicators.note: about means around, so the mixed letters surround the zero
in places the abbreviation inside the word for fashion

parts.note: mode is fashion
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A man about town hums a tuneless song about there being nothing new in fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: The scrambled letters wrap round the O, and the N then sits inside MODE.
explanation.definitionFit: Homme du monde is French for a man of the world, a sophisticated man of fashionable society.

clue.text: Suffered terribly — diagnose scurvy?

indicators.note: scurvy means shabby or rotten, so the letters are in a sorry state and reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sailor went through agony before the doctor identified scurvy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scurvy' looks like the disease being diagnosed; here it is the old adjective for contemptible.
explanation.definitionFit: To agonise is to endure great pain or anguish, so agonised is a past form of suffering badly.

clue.text: Sells, as opposed to retaining odd piece

indicators.note: to retain is to hold within, so the short word encloses the piece

parts.note: vs is the abbreviation of versus, against
an end is a leftover scrap, as in odds and ends

explanation.surface: A trader who sells off stock rather than keeping the odd item.
explanation.definitionFit: To vend is to offer goods for sale, so vends is a plain synonym of sells.

clue.text: Claret? What it may pour from with first cut in wound or vein (8, two words)

indicators.note: in places the shortened vessel inside the twisted letters
wound is the past of wind, so the letters that follow are twisted round

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the first letter is cut off, so the vessel loses its opening letter

parts.note: wine may be poured from a jug

explanation.surface: Claret, slang for blood, may pour from a cut, whether a wound or a vein.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound' looks like an injury but is the past of wind; claret is also boxing slang for blood, which steers the solver to cuts rather than to wine poured at table.
explanation.definitionFit: Vin rouge is French for red wine, and claret is red Bordeaux; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: Very good waterproof seal becoming loose

parts.note: 'So!' is an exclamation of approval, like 'very good'
lute is a clay or cement packed into joints to make them watertight

explanation.surface: Praise for a good waterproof seal, spoilt by the news that it is coming away.
explanation.walkthrough: SOLUTE here is the botanical adjective, not the chemist's noun for a dissolved substance.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany solute means loose or free, not adhering, so a part becoming detached is solute.

clue.text: Expose bum doctor, no longer sober

parts.note: MO is a medical officer
on is colloquial for tipsy

explanation.surface: A drunken doctor drops his trousers at the party.
explanation.definitionFit: To moon is the prank of baring the buttocks at someone, which exposes the bum.

clue.text: Worthless page filling I try in rags

indicators.note: something filling another sits inside it, so the page sign goes within
torn to rags means ripped into bits and jumbled, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
P is the abbreviation for page

explanation.surface: A writer padding out a page of a scruffy newspaper with worthless copy.
explanation.walkthrough: TRIPY is a colloquial adjective from tripe, rubbish; 'rags' in the surface means cheap newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe is slang for rubbish, so tripy writing is of no value at all.

clue.text: Year up north a drag? Absolutely, nothing less

indicators.note: less means without, so a nought is dropped from the slang word

parts.note: a tow is a pull or drag
mondo is slang for very or absolutely

explanation.surface: A grumble that a year in the north is an utter drag, nothing less.
explanation.walkthrough: MONDO loses its final O, the 'nothing', to give MOND. 'Up north' marks a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Towmond is a Scots and northern dialect word for a twelvemonth, a year.

clue.text: Plumb on half a hoist

parts.note: plumb means perpendicular, straight down, which is sheer
in cricket the on side is also the leg side

explanation.surface: A plumb line dangling from one side of a lifting rig.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side is the half of the field behind the batsman's legs, called the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheerlegs are a hoist made of two spars lashed at the top; one spar is a sheerleg.

clue.text: Mental state that's reverse of help with essay?

indicators.note: reverse asks for the word for help to be written back to front

parts.note: aid is help
a thesis is a long essay

explanation.surface: A student asks what frame of mind is the opposite of getting help with an essay.
explanation.definitionFit: Diathesis is a constitutional predisposition or habit of body or mind, a settled mental condition.

clue.text: What sounds like tuppenny pipe?

indicators.note: sounds like says the answer is heard, not spelt, as the word for tuppenny

parts.note: tuppenny means worth twopence, very cheap

explanation.surface: A riddle about what a twopenny tin whistle sounds like.
explanation.walkthrough: Tuppenny is British for costing twopence; the question mark warns that pipe is the verb a small bird does, not a tube.
explanation.definitionFit: To pipe is to make a thin high sound, as a young bird does when it chirps.

clue.text: One who's seriously disturbed others: a disturbance in part only

indicators.note: only a part of the following words is wanted, a run of letters across them

parts.note: the run starts at the last letter of the first word and ends four letters into the last

explanation.surface: Someone badly upset others and caused a fuss, though only in a small way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'others' seems to belong to the definition, but its last letter starts the hidden run.
explanation.definitionFit: A sadist takes pleasure in cruelty, a serious disturbance of the mind.

clue.text: Suggestion to 'elp where players learn introductory piece

indicators.note: dropping the aitch as in 'elp means the opening H goes too

parts.note: a hint is a suggestion
RADA is the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art, a London drama school

explanation.surface: A tip for anyone wanting a leg-up into drama school: start with an opening piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elp is help said with a dropped aitch, telling the solver to drop the H from the suggestion as well.
explanation.definitionFit: An intrada is an introductory or opening movement in music, a kind of prelude.

clue.text: Paint solvent? Ten litres will shift this, set

indicators.note: shifting things moves them about, so the letters of the measure are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
the word meant to be the leftover beside the answer once the measure is rearranged

explanation.surface: Ten litres of this paint solvent will shift the set paint.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: TEN LITRES should be the answer plus 'set' rearranged, but beside TRILENE it holds only S and T, so as printed the clue is one E short.
explanation.definitionFit: Trilene is a trade name for trichloroethylene, a solvent used to strip paint and degrease; the question mark marks the brand name.

clue.text: Fair skier in a tangle round end of slalom

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the tangled letters enclose the last letter
a tangle is a muddle, so the skier's letters are twisted into another order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, the only one wanted

parts.note: the final letter of slalom

explanation.surface: A skier with blond hair has come to grief at the last gate of the slalom course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair' looks like an adjective for the skier's hair or conduct; it is the noun, a fete.
explanation.definitionFit: A kermis is an annual outdoor fair or festival in the Low Countries, originally held at a church's dedication.

clue.text: One with stamina wasted year's time inside

indicators.note: inside places the abbreviation for time within the rearranged letters
something wasted is ruined, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An endurance athlete squandered a year of training time.
explanation.definitionFit: A stayer is a horse or runner with the stamina for long distances.

clue.text: Most loathsome trio of couples in case

parts.note: three pairs make six, VI in Roman numerals
lest means in case, for fear that

explanation.surface: The most hateful thing is three pairs of something packed in a box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' looks like a container, but 'in case' is the conjunction meaning for fear that.
explanation.definitionFit: Vilest is the superlative of vile, meaning the most detestable or disgusting.

clue.text: Ray, obsessive, turning radio dial?

indicators.note: turning round sends the pair of words back to front

parts.note: ray is a spelling of re, the second note of the sol-fa scale
a nut is an obsessive enthusiast

explanation.surface: Ray, a fanatic, keeps twiddling the knob on the wireless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ray' looks like a man's name; it is the musical note. The question mark admits the definition is loose: a dial is the part of the set you tune with.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuner is the knob or circuit used to select a station on a radio set.

clue.text: Being sesquipedalian, possibly block opposition minutes?

parts.note: a ped is a natural lump or block of soil
antis are people who are against something
M is the abbreviation for minutes

explanation.surface: A sesquipedalian MP filibusters, using long words to block the opposition for minutes on end.
explanation.walkthrough: Sesquipedalian means given to very long words; 'possibly' warns that this is only one way of being a pedant.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedantism is showy fussiness over learning and correctness, of which fondness for long words is one example.

clue.text: Fish spawn's minimal unit raised at bottom of river

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means read upwards, so the unit goes backwards

parts.note: the smallest unit of fish spawn is a single egg

explanation.surface: A fish lifts a single egg of spawn from the riverbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at bottom of' places the reversed egg below the river in the column.
explanation.definitionFit: The pogge is the armed bullhead, a small spiny sea fish of northern Europe.

clue.text: Electron's path test restricts a little

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so the exam word closes round the small amount

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination
a bit is a little

explanation.surface: A physics exam question on electron paths tests students' knowledge only a little.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics and chemistry an orbital is the region round a nucleus where an electron is likely to be found.

clue.text: Rhythmical pattern in most alaaps

indicators.note: in means contained within, here within the run of the next two words

parts.note: the last letter of the first word and the first three of the second

explanation.surface: Most alaaps, the slow openings of Indian ragas, follow a rhythmic cycle.
explanation.walkthrough: An alaap is the unmetred opening of a raga, so the surface is itself about Indian music.
explanation.definitionFit: In Indian classical music a tala is a repeated rhythmic cycle of fixed beats.

clue.text: Old rustic carried line

parts.note: bore is the past tense of bear, to carry
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A peasant of former times lugged a fishing line about.
explanation.definitionFit: Borel is an archaic word for a countryman or layman, unlearned and rustic.

clue.text: Presses clutch?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: urges on, as in egging someone on
second meaning: a set of birds' young-to-be laid together

explanation.surface: Pushes hard on the pedal, as a driver does with a car's clutch.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as driving; the question mark flags the bird's nest sense of clutch.
explanation.definitionFit: To egg on is to urge or press someone, and a clutch is a hen's nestful of eggs.

clue.text: Big eaters disposing of weighty amount?

definitions.text: Big eaters disposing of weighty amount?

indicators.note: disposing of something gets rid of it, so a heavy measure leaves the word

parts.note: gluttons eat to excess
tons are a heavy measure

explanation.surface: Hearty eaters putting away a huge quantity of food.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes the answer too: gluttons getting through tons of food are having a surfeit.
explanation.definitionFit: A glut is a surfeit, an excessive helping of food taken at once, as gluttons do.

clue.text: Nag replacing gin, machine length in press

indicators.note: replacing means one word is swapped in where the spirit stood

parts.note: an engine is a machine
taken as written; this is what comes out
taken as written; this goes in

explanation.surface: A racehorse breeder swaps gin for a horse, then a machine measures the press cutting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'press' means the printing press, not a newspaper or a squeeze.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennage is a printer's term for the number of ens in a piece of type matter, a measure of its length.

clue.text: E. Elgar composed bits of some symphonies without clobber

indicators.note: composed means put together, as music is written, so the letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: bits of the two words are just their opening letters

parts.note: the first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Edward Elgar wrote parts of some symphonies stark naked.
explanation.walkthrough: Clobber is British slang for clothes or kit, and gear is another word for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Clobber means gear or equipment, so being without it leaves one gearless.

clue.text: Shifting earth on coastal area I'd removed flower

indicators.note: shifting ground moves about, so the soil word's letters change places

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: removed means taken out, so the contracted 'I had' leaves the coastal word

parts.note: the seaside is the area beside the coast
the contraction written without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: A gardener on a crumbling seaside cliff has lost a favourite bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' means placed after, as in an across answer one part follows the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartsease is the wild pansy, Viola tricolor, a small garden and hedgerow bloom.
